subject: Re: IP claim notice & procurement approval path for AtlasBio order form
messages:
From: Ava Li <ava.li@atlasbio.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: procurements@atlasbio.com
Date: Sun, 19 Oct 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: IP claim notice language in order form - next steps

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are close on procurement but our legal team flagged the indemnity/third‑party IP language in the Order Form (section 7) as too broad for our regulator. A few items they asked us to confirm before signing: 

- Who controls defense for third‑party IP claims that arise from customer data / prompts?
- Whether Redwood will accept liability for claims arising from AtlasBio fine‑tuning on our dataset, or whether responsibility stays with AtlasBio.
- A narrow evidence list and notice windows so we can comply with our vendor management policy.

We attached the procurement team's PO and a redline of the Order Form for your reference (see attachments). Can we set a short call tomorrow to align legal trenches and procurement approvals? If possible we need an internal path to escalate if legal asks for an SLA exception or a cap change.

Best,
Ava Li
Head of Procurement | AtlasBio
attachments: PO-Atlas-9876.pdf (pdf), Atlas_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (docx)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Oct 2025 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: IP claim notice language in order form - next steps

Kimberly / Marissa —

Looping you in on AtlasBio's redlines. Quick ask: can legal propose a tight compromise so procurement can sign by the end of next week? Key constraints from the buyer: defender control sensitivity, carveout for customer‑fine‑tuning, and a shorter notice/evidence window. 

Proposed internal positions (first pass):
- Defense control: Redwood proposes right to defend with option to step in and retain counsel; if AtlasBio requests Redwood to cede control for a specific third‑party claim, require mutual written agreement plus indemnity for incremental costs.
- Fine‑tuning carveout: If AtlasBio fine‑tunes using their own data and we host model weights without modifications to base model, AtlasBio bears responsibility for claims tied solely to their dataset; Redwood remains responsible for claims arising from model base IP defects.
- Evidence/notice: 30 days notice to respond + evidence checklist limited to a defined set of items (samples, sample prompts, claim notice, contact points).

Can you draft a response that: 1) accepts a limited cap but keeps exceptions for willful misconduct; 2) narrows the evidence request; 3) proposes a 60‑day negotiation window for any SLA/cap exceptions that require leadership approval?

If this needs exec approval, copy me and I'll escalate to Legal Head and CRO.

Thanks — Jonas
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: IP claim notice language in order form - next steps

Jonas / team —

Thanks for the summary. Draft reply below — I've kept options where procurement can choose a cap band and where leadership signoff is required. Marked sections that are negotiable.

----- DRAFT TO ATLASBIO LEGAL -----
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Ava Li <ava.li@atlasbio.com>, counsel@atlasbio-legal.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IP claim notice language in order form - next steps

Ava / counsel —

Appreciate the flag and the clear redline. Redwood's suggested compromise is below: 

1) Defense control: Redwood will have the right to assume defense and control of third‑party IP claims that allege the model or hosted service infringes a third party's intellectual property. If AtlasBio reasonably requests Redwood to cede defense control for a specific claim, parties will negotiate in good faith; any agreement to cede control will require AtlasBio to reimburse Redwood for reasonable defense costs incurred after such concession.

2) Fine‑tuning carveout: Claims arising solely from AtlasBio supplied training/fine‑tuning data (including customer prompts or datasets) will be excluded from Redwood indemnity; AtlasBio will retain responsibility for those claims. Conversely, claims arising from defects in the base model or Redwood modifications to that model remain the responsibility of Redwood.

3) Cap and exceptions: Redwood is willing to accept a monetary cap on direct damages tied to the Order Form value tier (e.g., 1x–3x annual fees for higher tiers). Willful misconduct and gross negligence will remain uncapped. Any requested change to cap beyond the pre‑agreed band will require Legal + Commercial leadership approval and may trigger an SLA/price adjustment.

4) Notice & evidence: AtlasBio will provide written notice within 30 days of becoming aware of a claim. Redwood may request a limited set of evidence (see attached template) necessary to triage (claim notice, implicated inputs, timestamps, representative samples). Redwood will not request broad production of customer data beyond narrowly tailored samples.

Next steps: If this aligns, we can provide a redline to your Order Form track changes and a short addendum with the evidence checklist. If your procurement needs an exec signoff path for cap exceptions, please confirm the internal contact and timeline.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
attachments: evidence_request_template.pdf (pdf)
----- end draft -----


Marissa — can you confirm whether procurement will accept a banded cap or whether they need a firm number? If they need a firm number, we'll line up Legal Head for approval which may delay signing by a week.

Kimberly

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Ava Li <ava.li@atlasbio.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: IP claim notice language in order form - next steps

Ava / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Kimberly — this reads like a workable path. Procurement confirms AtlasBio will accept a banded cap tied to the order size (we'll provide the preferred band: 1x annual fees for standard pilot, 2x for enterprise). We also appreciate the explicit fine‑tuning carveout language — that addresses our risk office concern.

Two small asks from procurement: 
- Can Redwood commit to a named point of contact for evidence triage (email + phone)? Our security team requires a single liaison for the 30‑day window.
- If there's any change that requires exec approval, please flag and include an estimated timeline so we can manage our signoff queue.

If you're good with that, we'll accept the proposed redline and route for final PO signoff today.

Best,
Ava Li
Head of Procurement | AtlasBio
attachments: PO-Atlas-9876.pdf (pdf)

-----
Internal note: Jonas — procurement approved conditionally. No exec escalation required assuming we accept the cap band. Please confirm final redline and I'll trigger DocuSign.
